mainTopic: Drained drops and the storekeeper on ערב שבת, and a child sent shopping who breaks the jug and loses the change
overview: This amud opens with a question from a משנה about תרומה, which says that the drops drained from a tilted vessel count as תרומה. The answer, in the name of רבי אבהו, is that in an ordinary sale the seller keeps those last drops only because the buyer gives up hope on them (יאוש בעלים). Next, the גמרא asks whether רבי יהודה's ruling about a חנווני on ערב שבת is a קולא or a חומרא. A ברייתא shows it is a חומרא: the storekeeper is excused only at nightfall on ערב שבת, because he is busy then. Then a new משנה brings a new case. A father sends his young son to a storekeeper, and the boy breaks the jug and loses the change. The חכמים make the storekeeper pay, and רבי יהודה exempts him. The גמרא asks why the storekeeper should pay for a jug the father himself gave to a child. רב הושעיא and then רבה and רב יוסף each explain the case, but each explanation is challenged. The amud ends as אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין begin a new explanation, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: A question from the משנה about drained-out תרומה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a משנה about תרומה which suggests that drops drained from a tilted vessel go with what was poured out, and not to the original owner. This seems to clash with our משנה, which gives such drops to the seller.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't we learn in a משנה: If he tilted the vessel and drained it, that is תרומה!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges our משנה's rule that drops drained from a tilted vessel belong to the seller. It brings a משנה about תרומה that seems to say the opposite.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Our משנה says that if the seller tilts the vessel and drains out the last bits, those bits are his. The תרומה משנה says that when you tilt and drain a vessel of תרומה, those last bits count as תרומה, part of what was poured over. So the drained drops seem to go with the liquid that was transferred, and not stay with the one who poured.

keyTerms.meaning: He tilted it (the vessel) on its side
He drained it out completely
The portion of produce given to a כהן

phrases.english: But didn't we learn: If he tilted it and drained it,
phrases.notes: This is a משנה in תרומות. It talks about pouring תרומה oil or wine from one vessel into another.

phrases.english: this is תרומה!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the earlier line of our משנה that drained drops belong to the seller.
steps.kashyaTarget: Our משנה's rule: הרכינה ומיצה, the drained drops belong to the seller.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The תרומה משנה treats drained drops as part of the transferred liquid. That seems to mean they do not stay with the one who pours, so how can our משנה give them to the seller?

steps.title: The answer: the buyer gives up hope on tiny drops
steps.stepSummary: Using רבי אבהו's explanation, the גמרא answers that the seller keeps the drops only because the buyer gives up on such a small amount. That reason does not apply to תרומה.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: But wasn't it already said about this? רבי אבהו said: Because the owners give up hope, the חכמים dealt with it this way.
steps.whatsHappening: The question is answered with a teaching of רבי אבהו. He explains that the seller keeps the drained drops because the buyer gives up hope on them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Strictly speaking, the last drops do belong to the buyer, just like in the תרומה משנה. But a buyer doesn't care about a few tiny drops and gives up on them (יאוש בעלים), so the חכמים let the seller keep them. With תרומה, giving up hope can't change anything, because the drops still have the holy status of תרומה, so they remain תרומה.

keyTerms.meaning: But wasn't it already said about this? (pointing to an existing explanation)
The owner giving up hope on his property
They (the חכמים) dealt with it, ruling about it this way

steps.confusionAlert: Don't think the two משניות really disagree about who owns the drops. Both agree the drops are really part of what is transferred. Our משנה gives them to the seller only because of the buyer's יאוש.
steps.whatToRemember: The seller keeps the drained drops only because the buyer gives up on them (יאוש בעלים). For תרומה, giving up hope doesn't matter, so the drops stay תרומה.

phrases.english: He said to him: But wasn't it said about it,
phrases.notes: "It" is our משנה's rule that the drained drops belong to the seller.

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
Because of the owners' giving up hope, they dealt with it.
phrases.notes: The "owners" here are the buyers. They don't bother about a few last drops.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: הָא אִיתְּמַר עֲלַהּ, אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge from the תרומה משנה.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Distinguishes the cases by giving the reason behind our משנה's rule (יאוש בעלים), a reason that does not apply to תרומה.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Our משנה seemed to say the drained drops legally belong to the seller, which clashes with the תרומה משנה.
steps.terutzMaskana: The drops really belong with the transferred liquid. The seller keeps them only because the buyer gives up hope, and that changes nothing for the status of תרומה.

steps.title: Is רבי יהודה being lenient or strict?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the next line of the משנה, about a storekeeper, and asks a question. Does רבי יהודה's ruling about ערב שבת go back to the first part of the משנה as a leniency, or to the last part as a stringency?
steps.simpleTranslation: The משנה says: And a storekeeper does not have to drip out the last drops, etc. They asked: Is רבי יהודה talking about the first part, and being lenient? Or maybe he is talking about the last part, and being strict?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a new topic. It quotes the משנה about a חנווני and asks which part of the משנה רבי יהודה is responding to.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first part (רישא) says a seller must let three drops drip out. If רבי יהודה is talking about that, he is adding a קולא: on ערב שבת at nightfall the seller is excused. The last part (סיפא) says a storekeeper never has to drip. If רבי יהודה is talking about that, he is adding a חומרא: a storekeeper is excused only on ערב שבת at nightfall, and the rest of the time he must drip.

keyTerms.meaning: A storekeeper
To let the last drops drip out to the buyer
A question was asked among them (an open question)
The first part / the last part of a משנה
A leniency / a stringency

steps.confusionAlert: Both sides of the question agree on what רבי יהודה said. The only question is which earlier line of the משנה he is reacting to, and that decides whether his words make the law easier or harder.

phrases.english: "And the storekeeper is not obligated to drip, etc."
phrases.notes: The "etc." stands for the rest of the משנה line: רבי יהודה says that on ערב שבת at nightfall he is exempt.

phrases.english: A question was raised before them:
Is Rabbi Yehuda referring to the first clause, and being lenient;
or perhaps he refers to the last clause, and is being strict?

steps.triggerLanguage: אִיבַּעְיָא לְהוּ: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה – אַרֵישָׁא קָאֵי, וּלְקוּלָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next line of the משנה, opening a new topic.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Whether רבי יהודה's ערב שבת exemption is a leniency added to the רישא (the seller must drip) or a stringency added to the סיפא (the storekeeper is always exempt).

steps.title: A ברייתא shows רבי יהודה is being strict
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא quotes רבי יהודה saying the storekeeper is exempt on ערב שבת at nightfall because he is busy. This shows he was limiting the storekeeper's exemption, so his ruling is a stringency on the סיפא.
steps.simpleTranslation: Come and hear, as a ברייתא teaches: רבי יהודה says: On ערב שבת at nightfall, a storekeeper is exempt, because a storekeeper is busy.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question with a ברייתא. In it, רבי יהודה names the storekeeper and gives a reason that fits only ערב שבת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יהודה specifically says the חנווני is exempt on ערב שבת because he is busy then. That means at other times the storekeeper is not exempt and must drip. So רבי יהודה is responding to the סיפא and being strict, not lenient.

keyTerms.meaning: As it gets dark, at nightfall
Busy, under pressure

steps.whatToRemember: רבי יהודה is strict: a storekeeper must normally drip the last drops. He is excused only on ערב שבת at nightfall, when he is busy.
steps.whyThisMatters: The reason "he is busy" explains the rule. The exemption depends on the special rush before שבת, not on storekeepers in general.

phrases.english: Come and hear: As it is taught in a baraita,

phrases.aramaic: רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר: עֶרֶב שַׁבָּת עִם חֲשֵׁכָה –
phrases.english: Rabbi Yehuda says: On Shabbat eve at nightfall,
a storekeeper is exempt,
because the storekeeper is busy.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּא שְׁמַע: דְּתַנְיָא, רַבִּי יְהוּדָה אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question by bringing a ברייתא.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבי יהודה is referring to the סיפא and being strict: a storekeeper is exempt only on ערב שבת at nightfall, because he is busy then.

steps.title: The new משנה: a child sent to the storekeeper breaks the jug and loses the change
steps.stepSummary: A father sends his son to a storekeeper with a פונדיון. The storekeeper gives oil and an איסר in change. The boy breaks the jug and loses the coin. The חכמים say the storekeeper is liable, and רבי יהודה exempts him. Everyone agrees he is exempt if the jug was in the child's hand and the storekeeper poured the oil into it.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: A man sends his son to a storekeeper with a פונדיון (a coin worth two איסרים). The storekeeper measures out one איסר's worth of oil and gives the boy the other איסר as change. The boy breaks the jug and loses the איסר. The storekeeper must pay. רבי יהודה exempts him, because the father sent the boy for exactly this purpose. The חכמים agree with רבי יהודה when the jug was in the child's hand and the storekeeper poured the oil into it. In that case the storekeeper is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה starts with a new case. A young child is sent shopping and loses everything, and the תנאים argue whether the storekeeper has to pay.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A small child is not trusted to look after things. So the question is whether handing goods to the child counts as giving them to the father. The חכמים say it does not, so the storekeeper is still responsible. רבי יהודה says the father sent the child to bring things back, so handing them to the child is enough.

keyTerms.meaning: Storekeeper
A coin worth two איסרים
A small coin, half a פונדיון
A small jug or flask
A young child, not yet responsible

steps.confusionAlert: In the concession at the end, the child brought the jug himself and held it while the oil was poured. In the main case, the storekeeper handed the jug over to the child.

phrases.english: MISHNA
One who sends his son to a storekeeper
with a pundeyon in his hand,
phrases.notes: A פונדיון is worth two איסרים. That's why there is change left over.

phrases.english: and he measured out for him an issar's worth of oil
and gave him the issar,
phrases.notes: This is the second איסר, given back as change.

phrases.aramaic: שָׁבַר אֶת הַצְּלוֹחִית וְאִבֵּד אֶת הָאִיסָּר –
phrases.english: and the boy broke the jug and lost the issar
the storekeeper is liable.
Rabbi Yehuda exempts him,
because the father sent him for exactly this.
And the Sages agree with Rabbi Yehuda
when the jug is in the child's hand
and the storekeeper measured the oil into it
that the storekeeper is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה after the previous discussion of the storekeeper and ערב שבת.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חכמים: the storekeeper is liable for the broken jug and lost coin. רבי יהודה: he is exempt, since the father sent the child to bring them back. Everyone agrees he is exempt if the child held the jug while the oil was poured.

steps.title: Why would the storekeeper pay for the father's own jug?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא understands the argument about the oil and the איסר: did the father send the boy only to place an order, or to carry things home? But the jug belonged to the father, who handed it to the child himself. Its loss is his own fault, so why should the storekeeper pay?
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: About the איסר and the oil, the argument makes sense. The חכמים hold that the father sent the boy only to let the storekeeper know what he wanted. רבי יהודה holds that he sent the boy so the storekeeper would send the goods back with him. But when the boy broke the jug, that is a loss the father caused knowingly!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא accepts the reasoning for the oil and the coin. Then it challenges the חכמים about the jug.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The oil and the coin were given to the child by the storekeeper, so the חכמים can blame him. But the jug was the father's, and the father himself trusted it to a small child. When an owner knowingly puts his own item at risk like that, nobody else has to pay for it.

keyTerms.meaning: It makes sense regarding... (sets up a contrast with a difficulty)
He sent him only to let the storekeeper know
He sent him so the goods would be sent back with him
A loss the owner knowingly caused, which no one else must pay for

steps.whyThisMatters: This sets up the main question of the סוגיא: whose jug was it, and on what terms was it in the storekeeper's hands?

phrases.english: GEMARA
It makes sense regarding the issar and the oil,
they argue about this:
the Rabbis hold:
he sent him only to let the storekeeper know,
and Rabbi Yehuda holds:
he sent him so that the storekeeper would send the goods back with him;
but when he broke the jug
that is a loss caused knowingly!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the חכמים's ruling in the new משנה, specifically about the jug.
steps.kashyaTarget: The חכמים's ruling that the storekeeper pays for the broken jug.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The jug was the father's, and he himself gave it to an irresponsible child. That makes it an אבדה מדעת, which the storekeeper should not have to cover.

steps.title: רב הושעיא: the father was selling the jug, and the storekeeper took it to examine
steps.stepSummary: רב הושעיא says the father sold jugs and sent one with his son in case the storekeeper wanted to buy it. The storekeeper took it to look it over. Following שמואל, someone who takes an item to examine it is responsible even for accidents.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב הושעיא said: Here we are dealing with a homeowner who sells jugs, and the storekeeper took the jug to examine it. This follows שמואל, who said: One who takes a vessel from a craftsman in order to examine it, and it is destroyed by accident while in his hands, is liable.
steps.whatsHappening: רב הושעיא answers the question about the jug. The storekeeper had taken responsibility for it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Once the storekeeper took the jug to examine it, it was no longer just the father's risk. It was like a borrowed item in the storekeeper's hands, and שמואל says such a person pays even for accidents. So handing it back to a child did not end his responsibility, and it is not an אבדה מדעת.

keyTerms.meaning: A private homeowner, not a professional merchant
In order to examine it before deciding to buy
A craftsman
Was lost or destroyed by an accident beyond one's control

phrases.english: Rav Hoshaya said:

phrases.aramaic: הָכָא בְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת מוֹכֵר צְלוֹחִיּוֹת עָסְקִינַן,
phrases.english: Here we are dealing with a homeowner who sells jugs,
phrases.notes: The homeowner is the father. He sent the jug along in case the storekeeper wanted to buy it.

phrases.english: and where the storekeeper took it
in order to examine it;
and this follows Shmuel,
for Shmuel said:
One who takes a vessel from a craftsman
in order to examine it,
and it was destroyed by accident in his hands
is liable.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב הוֹשַׁעְיָא הָכָא בְּבַעַל הַבַּיִת מוֹכֵר צְלוֹחִיּוֹת עָסְקִינַן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 6 by redefining the case.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Redefining the case (אוקימתא) and supporting it with a ruling of an אמורא
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The jug was simply the father's container, so its loss is his own fault.
steps.terutzMaskana: The jug was the father's merchandise, taken by the storekeeper to examine. Like שמואל, he is responsible for it even for accidents.

steps.title: Would שמואל's ruling then depend on an argument between תנאים?
steps.stepSummary: If רב הושעיא is right, רבי יהודה exempts the storekeeper even though he took the jug to examine it. That means רבי יהודה disagrees with שמואל, and שמואל's rule would only follow the חכמים. The גמרא does not want to say that.
steps.simpleTranslation: Shall we say that שמואל's ruling is a dispute between תנאים?!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pushes back on רב הושעיא's answer. His reading would make שמואל's ruling the subject of an argument between תנאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In רב הושעיא's version, the חכמים make the storekeeper pay because they agree with שמואל, while רבי יהודה exempts him. That would mean רבי יהודה rejects שמואל's rule. The גמרא prefers an explanation where both תנאים can agree with שמואל.

keyTerms.meaning: Shall we say...? (often suggests something we would rather not say)
It is a matter of dispute between תנאים

phrases.english: Shall we say that Shmuel's ruling is a dispute between Tannaim?!
phrases.notes: He means רבי יהודה would be disagreeing with שמואל, and the גמרא doesn't want that.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges רב הושעיא's answer from step 7.
steps.kashyaTarget: רב הושעיא's explanation of the משנה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: His reading forces רבי יהודה to disagree with שמואל, making שמואל's ruling depend on a מחלוקת תנאים. We prefer not to say that.

steps.title: רבה and רב יוסף: the storekeeper sold the jug too
steps.stepSummary: רבה and רב יוסף explain that the storekeeper sold the jug along with the oil, so the jug was his merchandise. The jug is then just like the oil and the coin. רבי יהודה and the חכמים each follow their own view about why the father sent the boy.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבה and רב יוסף both say: Here we are dealing with a storekeeper who sells jugs. רבי יהודה follows his own reasoning, and the חכמים follow theirs.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא drops רב הושעיא's approach and gives a new explanation from רבה and רב יוסף. In their version, the jug belonged to the storekeeper.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the jug came from the storekeeper, it is not an אבדה מדעת of the father at all. The jug falls into the same argument as the oil and the coin. The חכמים say the boy was sent only to place the order, so the storekeeper should not have handed him anything. רבי יהודה says the boy was sent to bring the goods back, so the storekeeper is exempt. שמואל's ruling plays no part, so no תנא disagrees with him.

keyTerms.meaning: Both of them
Follows his own line of reasoning

steps.whatToRemember: In the view of רבה and רב יוסף, the jug was sold by the storekeeper, so the jug, the oil and the coin are all one argument: the חכמים say the child was sent only to place the order, and רבי יהודה says he was sent to bring things back. The next step challenges this explanation, and the גמרא then drops it.

phrases.english: Rather, Rabba and Rav Yosef
who both say:
Here we are dealing with a storekeeper who sells jugs;
and Rabbi Yehuda follows his own reasoning,
and the Rabbis follow theirs.
phrases.notes: These are the two reasons from step 6: sent only to place the order, or sent to bring the goods back.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא רַבָּה וְרַב יוֹסֵף דְּאָמְרִי תַּרְוַיְיהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces רב הושעיא's answer, which was challenged in step 8, with a new answer to the קשיא of step 6.
steps.terutzResolutionType: A different redefinition of the case (אוקימתא)
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The jug belonged to the father, so its loss seemed to be his own fault. Or, following רב הושעיא, the argument seemed to depend on שמואל's rule.
steps.terutzMaskana: The jug was the storekeeper's merchandise. Its loss falls under the same argument as the oil and the coin, and שמואל is not involved.

steps.title: The last clause of the משנה does not fit the explanation of רבה and רב יוסף
steps.stepSummary: If the חכמים hold that the father sent the boy only to place an order, why do they agree that the storekeeper is exempt when he poured oil into the child's jug?
steps.simpleTranslation: If that is so, look at the last clause: the חכמים agree with רבי יהודה that when the jug was in the child's hand and the storekeeper measured oil into it, the storekeeper is exempt. But you said that, according to the חכמים, the father sent the boy only to let the storekeeper know what he wanted!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer of רבה and רב יוסף from Step 9. It points to the last line of the משנה, which does not seem to fit that answer.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Under רבה and רב יוסף, the חכמים hold the storekeeper liable because the father sent the boy only to place an order, not to carry anything home. If so, giving oil to the child should be the storekeeper's mistake in every case, even when he poured it into the child's jug. Yet the משנה says the חכמים agree he is exempt in that case. That contradicts the reason given for their view.

keyTerms.meaning: If so: if your explanation is correct
Say the last clause: look at the end of the משנה
They agree / concede
A jug or flask
He sent him only to inform, meaning only to place the order

steps.confusionAlert: The גמרא is not asking about רבי יהודה here. The problem is that the חכמים themselves agree to exempt the storekeeper, even though their reason should make him liable.

phrases.english: If so, say the last clause:
phrases.notes: This is the "everyone agrees" line of the משנה from Step 5.

phrases.english: The Rabbis concede to Rabbi Yehuda
when the jug is in the hand of the child,
and the storekeeper measured the oil into it,
that the storekeeper is exempt.
But you said he sent him only to inform!
phrases.notes: "You" means רבה and רב יוסף, who said the חכמים hold the boy was sent only to place the order.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks the answer of רבה and רב יוסף in Step 9 using the last clause of the משנה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The explanation of רבה and רב יוסף that the חכמים hold the father sent the boy only to place the order.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: If the boy was sent only to place the order, handing him oil is always the storekeeper's fault. The חכמים's agreement to exempt the storekeeper when he poured into the child's jug therefore contradicts their supposed reason.

steps.title: A new explanation begins from אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא drops the previous approach and opens a new way to explain the case in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, אביי בר אבין and רבי חנינא בר אבין both say: What case are we dealing with here?
steps.whatsHappening: The word אלא shows that the גמרא is giving up on the explanation of רבה and רב יוסף. It is setting up a new explanation, and the actual case will be described in the next lines.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge in Step 10 was strong enough that the גמרא does not try to defend the earlier answer. Two אמוראים will now define the case of the משנה in a different way, one that should avoid both the problem with שמואל and the problem from the last clause.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather: the previous answer is dropped
Both of them
What case are we dealing with here? This introduces a narrower picture of the case

phrases.english: Rather, Abaye bar Avin
and Rabbi Chanina bar Avin
